title: Rabbi Ada (or Rabbi Ida) of Caesarea
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman places Rabbi Ada of Caesarea among the third-generation Amoraim of the Land of Israel and identifies him as a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In Moed Katan 20b he recites a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan. He reports in Rabbi Yochanan’s name at the end of chapter 4 of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:4, and again at the end of Rosh Hashanah.

notes.text: The final locator סוף א״ה remains unresolved. The preceding verb describes this student teaching before Rabbi Yochanan.

The saved whole Guggenheimer RoshHashanah4:4 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Ada of Caesarea in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Whole4:10:5 has another such report, a candidate for the chapter-end pointer rather than proof of the letters סוף א״ה; those letters stay unresolved. The student’s שתני קמיה means recitation before his teacher, not anonymous plural teachers. MoedKatan20b and Berakhotend4 were not newly inspected; the third-generation and teacher reconstruction are Hyman’s account. Ida remains a heading alternative; only the named Ada form has a new full-title comparison.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 105) gives the alternative Ida in the heading and reads “the end of Rosh Hashanah” (סוף ר״ה), where the supplied transcription has סוף א״ה. The report in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:10:5 parallels the report at the end of Berakhot chapter 4. The recitation in Moed Katan names Ada and concerns news of a relative’s death received on Shabbat. The classification by generation is Hyman’s.
